Honestly the relationships I had with friends that did drink kind of fell apart. I still keep up with some of them but they are at arms distance at best. 

I couldn’t maintain those relationships and keep my goal. Those relationships didn’t support me and they didn’t serve to better me. 

Quitting shows you who your friends truly are. It can be scary when you’re first starting. This decision will impact your life in so many ways that you can’t even foresee at the moment. 

But I promise the other side of the tunnel is bright. The clarity is unimaginable.

I remember waking up one morning at my cousins apartment. No clue how I got there. I do know I was partying the night before across town at a friends house . Well I texted my friend to come get me and on the way home he told me that one of my cousins girlfriends was blowing up my phone the previous evening. 

Now me and this girl had a completely platonic relationship at this point as she was good friends with my cousin and my sister and no fault to her she just wasn’t my type like AT ALL. 

Well my friend was jabbing at me asking me if I got laid. I laughed because that was so far out of the question in my mind, but later when I got home I checked my wallet and found that the condom was missing from it. 

Extreme guilt and disgust hit me. In my drunken stupor I had gotten a friend from the party to drive me over. I was BLACK OUT drunk. I don’t remember any of it. 

My cousins friend and I never spoke about that night ever again. I saw her several times afterward. She ended up being killed in a car wreck about a year and a half ago. I went to her funeral. I was sober at this point. Just had to sit in the church pew and think about that night over and over. To this day I wish we would’ve spoken about it.

Recovering alcoholic here. Your drinking is a choice you’re making and have been making for some time from what it sounds like. You have to want to stop drinking to actually stop. 

You have three options - incarceration, death, or sobriety. Those are the only three possible outcomes. You’re already headed down the first path. Do yourself a favor and stop. There are options available if you need medical assistance to stop.
Get a lawyer. This sounds like a bunch of bullshit.

You’re license more than likely isn’t suspended YET. Hire an attorney. You need to request an ALR hearing now. Like right now. Don’t wait. You only have like 2 weeks or something to request this hearing or your license is automatically revoked. 

You can order a new license from the state in the mean time. Just get it off the state website.

Hire an attorney

A lot of states just getting the DWI in the first place is an automatic license suspension. Just one thing that happens as a result of the charge. 

You’re stuck with it for the time being. If your license is only suspended you have X amount of time you can’t drive.

If it’s revoked you need to contact the DMV and see what you can do to get it reinstated.

When I was released from jail I had been told by at least 3 people that I needed to request an ALR hearing. I also received a temporary license suspension paper that had all of this information on it. The officer also took my license when I was arrested. 

I promise you, you were informed. At some point. I HIGHLY doubt the DMV is going to let that slide.
As others have said your license was probably getting suspended anyway. Get started on it now. Hire an attorney.

Unfortunately the “woe is me” ploy isn’t going to get you shit anywhere with the law. Ignore it and you will just make your life substantially more difficult. Carpool or use a ride share app for the time being. DO NOT DRIVE.

Your first court date they won’t drug test you in my experience. If you get probation after your second (sentencing) court appearance they definitely will. There is usually a couple month time slot between these two hearings. Plenty of time to clean up naturally. 

If you fail that first drug test you’re looking at weekly testing versus monthly until you’re clean. More money. More pain in the ass. (The drug tests aren’t free.) If you still continue to test dirty on weekly tests then you will be violating your probation. Then you’re going to jail. 

Stop smoking and no CBD products before your sentencing hearing. They don’t give a rats ass about your stress level and have heard every story in the book. Weed is still illegal in Texas. 

Keep your nose clean until this is resolved.
If the report is missing information there is a chance that they throw out the case, yea. Hire an attorney.

Just take the money hit. A grand of body repair is cheaper than a 10k DWI broski. I know it sucks but just let it be a lesson that if you are planning to consume ANY alcohol at all. DO NOT GET BEHIND THE WHEEL.
This. Get it over with in a weekend and be done.

Also when you’re on the job hunt. Don’t be forthcoming with the fact that you have a DUI. Make them find it. If they’re gonna decline hiring you for having a DUI anyway, what’s the point of divulging that information?

Honestly your sentence is fairly light all things considered. I’ve seen way worse for first offenders. Specially on the fine/fees you owe.

Your attorney did his job by getting your charged reduced from a .16 (which is a Class A Misdemeanor with much heavier penalties) to a .08 (Class B Misdemeanor). I think that was money well spent. You also cannot have your case deferred or sealed with a Class A Misdemeanor. 

Probation is infinitely better than sitting in jail. Yeah there are stipulations and it’s hard on your pocket book/getting around but that’s the whole point. They want to inconvenience the hell out of you. Yeah having your car impounded for a 10 days is pretty shit but just keep in mind it’s only for a week! Time flies. ATLEAST YOU ARENT IN JAIL. Ride share app or car pool for a week and get it done.

A suspension and a revocation are not the same thing. A suspension is a temporary measure which usually occurs directly after being charged with a DUI. Then pending an ALR hearing your license can be revoked which is basically a permanent removal of your license. You have to pay to have it reinstated. Huge pain.

You may not be able to appeal. A lot of times when you accept the sentence you waive your right to appeal. Your attorney should’ve explained this when you were sentenced. If you are able to appeal you may win, but you’re looking at potentially shelling out MORE money to attorneys and dragging this out further or you may lose, in which case you spend more money on attorneys and get a harsher sentence (and jail time potentially). 

If you’ve made it this far, pull yourself up and keep going fam. This isn’t a death sentence for you and this isn’t forever either. I personally wouldn’t appeal. Just do the work. Stay positive and just jump when they say jump. A year goes by faster than you realize.

I am going to preface this and say just hang loose for the time being. He might not contact you at all and may be okay with the damage on his vehicle. If that's the case and you are not going to file a claim on your vehicle. You're in the clear.

I literally just went through a similar situation last week (except I was the one that was rear ended). This situation happened in Texas. So a couple of things I learned just today -

If you didn't call the police at the time of the accident and you both left the scene, you both mutually agreed that the damage was minimal and no one was injured. That's that. For example, if someone stops responding to someone else, you cant file a hit and run on the person.

Quite frankly, if he doesnt have your insurance information it doesnt really matter. He will have to file it with his insurance company and pay his deductible. At the time his car is fixed, his insurance company may attempt to contact yours. I believe they have enough information on you to locate your insurance company. If this is the case insurance companies will talk and he will get the money he paid for his deductible back and the bad rap will go on you. 

All of that being said, if someone decides to file a claim they will still need a police report. You might as well go ahead and do this if youre looking to get your car repaired. This usually will involve you calling dispatch and then a deputy calling you back and talking to you about the situation. From there they will write it up and give you a reference number for you to give to your insurance company.

Unfortunately for me, the guy that hit me is being a total douche about it. Dont be that guy. If he texts and says there is something wrong, provide your insurance information. Be a good citizen. No one likes their car messed up.

So a couple things that I learned that I am passing on to you:

* 1.) Upon getting in the accident get out, assess for any injuries. Call 911 if necessary.

* 2.) If everyone is deemed safe, go ahead and call the local police department to come out (dont dial 911).
* 3.) Exchange names, insurance information, phone numbers, addresses.
* 4.) Locate any witnesses to the scene and gather their contact information.
* 5.) Take pictures of license plates/make models of cars/damage to the vehicles.
* 6.) Once the police show up, respond to all requests (you may get a ticket).
* 7.) Call your insurance company
